data.title: JPM Benefits from Higher Rates, but Earnings Growth Is Slowing
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) is benefiting from higher rates, but earnings growth is slowing. Shares of the largest U.S. bank have outperformed the broader U.S. financials sector in 2026, as measured by popular ETFs such as the iShares U.S. Financials ETF (IYF). JPMorgan Chase, the world's largest bank by market share, is set to deliver earnings growth of about 21% in 2026, driven by strong performance in businesses benefiting from robust capital markets activity.

Looking ahead to 2027, analysts expect JPMorgan Chase to grow earnings per share (EPS) by only about 3%. I expect the benefits from higher interest rates to be somewhat offset by a normalization in asset management and investment banking performance.

Coupled with a premium valuation of 14.7x 2026 earnings, especially relative to U.S. banking peers, I believe this dynamic supports a Hold rating for JPMorgan Chase, somewhat more bearish than the Moderate Buy Wall Street consensus rating.

data.title: Why Are Tech Stocks GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN Falling in Premarket Today, Sept. 15?
data.description:
U.S. tech giants Alphabet (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT), and Amazon (AMZN) are down in premarket trading today. The move comes as U.S. Treasury yields climbed to their highest level since 2007 and remain above 5%. Investors are worried that oil prices staying above $100 could add to inflation and put more pressure on the economy. GOOGL and MSFT stock are down by 1%, while AMZN fell 0.50% as of this writing.

Traders are also turning their attention to the Federal Reserve and are expecting a quarter-point rate hike. The Federal Reserve's two-day September meeting starts Tuesday.

What Higher Yields Mean for Tech Stocks

Higher government bond yields can increase borrowing costs for consumers and businesses while making stocks less attractive compared with bonds. This can put pressure on high-growth tech stocks such as Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. Higher yields can also reduce the value investors place on future earnings, which may weigh on stock valuations.

They added that strong earnings have so far helped offset the pressure from higher interest rates. data.title: Musk Leaves Door Open to Tesla-SpaceX Merger as TSLA, SPCX Stocks Fall
data.description:
Elon Musk has given investors his clearest signal yet that he is open to combining Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX), though he stopped short of confirming that merger talks are underway.

Speaking at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on Monday, Musk was asked why Tesla and SpaceX remain separate despite growing cooperation between the two companies. He called it a "great question" and pointed to their expanding ties across several areas.

"With all this collaboration, on so many levels, who can imagine what action one might take when there's so much close collaboration in so many areas," Musk said. He did not give a timeline, deal structure, or commitment.

data.title: Citi Warns AI Safety Risks Could Threaten Stock Rally; Flags AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT
data.description:
Citigroup's head of U.S. equity trading strategy, Stuart Kaiser, warned that growing AI safety concerns could slow AI model development and weigh on corporate earnings, potentially putting pressure on U.S. stocks. Kaiser adopted a more cautious stance on equities, warning that slower AI progress could "crimp" earnings-per-share (EPS) revisions and weaken an important pillar of the market rally.

Citi also highlighted rising bond yields, surging oil prices, and the upcoming November midterm elections as potential headwinds for stocks. Citigroup expects the S&P 500 (SPX) to remain near its recent highs, although a 3%-5% pullback could attract buyers. Kaiser identified Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta (META), and Amazon (AMZN) as stocks that could be sensitive to these risks.

What Are the Key Headwinds for Stocks?

Here's how the three potential headwinds could impact the stock market:

Promotion

  • Rising bond yields: Higher yields can make bonds more attractive relative to stocks and put pressure on equity valuations, particularly high-growth stocks such as tech and AI.
  • Surging oil prices: Higher oil prices can fuel inflation, potentially increasing the chances of higher interest rates and squeezing corporate profit margins.
  • November midterm elections: Kaiser and his team believe Republicans could lose control of the House and Senate, potentially increasing market volatility. Companies tied to power generation and data centers could be particularly sensitive to potential policy changes.

Why Is Citi Growing Cautious on Stocks?

Kaiser noted that the S&P 500 fell 0.8% last week as investors focused on macroeconomic risks without the support of fresh earnings catalysts. He expects a challenging period ahead, citing a seasonally weak September and a higher bar for investors to re-engage with equities.

The bank expects the S&P 500 to remain within about 2% of its August highs, potentially keeping investors on the sidelines. A 3%-5% pullback could attract dip buyers, but the market may need to retest its all-time highs to trigger stronger buying.

Citi also warned that AI safety concerns could broadly weigh on investor sentiment, adding another layer of uncertainty for technology stocks.

AI Regulation in Focus

The AI safety debate intensified over the weekend after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman also dismissed the possibility of a 2026 IPO, while Elon Musk raised concerns about AI risks.

President Donald Trump, however, has opposed slowing AI development or imposing heavy regulation, arguing that the U.S. needs to maintain its technological advantage over China. He has dismissed some AI risk concerns as exaggerated while acknowledging that safeguards may still be needed.

data.title: President Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Live Onstage to Dismiss AI Safety Fears as a Hoax; NVDA Stock Drops 3.4%
data.description:
President Donald Trump phoned Nvidia (NVDA) Chief Executive Jensen Huang live on stage on Monday. Speaking to a room of tech investors at the All-In Summit, Trump told the crowd that fear over artificial intelligence is a hoax. Huang was in the middle of an on-stage talk when his phone rang. He placed the president on speakerphone so the audience could hear Trump's view on the tech market.

Trump argued that building large data centers brings great wealth to people and states. He noted that stopping AI work would play right into the hands of China. Huang agreed with the president during the call, stating that American firms will not let that happen. The phone call came after Trump posted on social media that strong leadership is the main safety tool the country needs, brushing off calls for strict government rules.

OpenAI and Anthropic Aim to Slowdown AI Model Updates

Nvidia shares fell despite the supportive words from the White House. Nvidia stock (NVDA) dropped nearly 3.4% on Monday afternoon to trade near $211.81. Other chipmakers took harder hits. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) slipped over 5%, while Intel (INTC) lost more than 5%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), a main fund tracking the chip sector, slid 6% as investors reacted to news from tech leaders.

Promotion

The market drop started after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman supported calls to slow down AI model development to test safety. Traders grew worried that a pause by major AI labs could mean smaller chip orders. Still, some investors noted that the sell-off might be short-term panic rather than a real drop in chip demand.

Nvidia Maintains Strong Revenue Streams

Even if big AI labs slow down their work, Nvidia maintains strong revenue backup. Unlike competitors that count on a few big buyers, Nvidia sells hardware to a wide range of growing startups and software groups. Nvidia recently signed a $12.9 billion deal to buy Hugging Face, a major open-source software platform. This purchase keeps millions of developers using Nvidia chips even if giant labs cut spending.

At the same time, new projects continue to drive long-term chip orders. SpaceX (SPCX) chief Elon Musk confirmed that SpaceX plans to launch AI data centers into space next year using Nvidia chips. Building space data centers helps bypass land and power limits on Earth.

data.title: Oracle's (ORCL) Q1 Still Didn't Prove the Value of Its Spending Spree
data.description:
Oracle's (ORCL) Q1 results made one thing clear: demand for its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is booming, but the actual value of its heavy spending spree remains completely unproven. Perhaps the best way to describe Oracle today is as a legacy software company spending like an AI infrastructure giant before proving it can earn like one.

Q1 reinforced that contrast. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) grew at a triple-digit rate, while backlog reached $664 billion. So while demand for AI compute is clearly not the problem, there is concern around the cost of meeting that demand.

Capex is surging, cash flow is under pressure, and Oracle still relies on debt, stock issuance, and customer prepayments to fund the buildout. That is hard to ignore without clearer evidence that these investments will generate strong enough returns. Proving that demand exists does not automatically mean that serving it will create enough value for shareholders.

Promotion

200% short exposure to AMZN with AMZO

After losing about half its market value in 12 months, ORCL is clearly cheaper. Yet, for me, it still needs to show returns. For now, I'm sticking with a Hold.

The Logic behind Oracle's Spending Spree

Think about the logic behind Oracle's spending spree. Oracle is a legacy software company that has spent years building its cloud infrastructure business. Then AI dramatically expanded the opportunity, creating extraordinary demand for compute and cloud capacity. Oracle realized it was increasingly well positioned to address that demand.

However, if Oracle relied only on cash generated by its legacy software business, it likely wouldn't be able to build capacity fast enough. It could also lose contracts to Amazon's (AMZN) AWS, Microsoft's (MSFT) Azure, Google (GOOGL), and other cloud providers.

So, basically, Oracle realized that its customers are ready to consume far more capacity than it currently has. If the expected returns on that capacity are attractive, it would make little sense to constrain growth simply because internally generated cash flow cannot fund the entire buildout.

As a result, debt, equity issuance, customer prepayments, and other funding sources have become tools for bringing future capacity forward. The bear case that has haunted Oracle — and helped wipe out roughly 50% of its market value over the past 12 months — begins exactly where this logic ends. The market is still asking one key question: What happens if Oracle is wrong about the economics of all this demand?

data.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Slowdown Calls Put Huge AI Spending in Focus
data.description:
OpenAI and Anthropic are calling for a slower pace of frontier AI development just as the financial cost of staying at the frontier is becoming enormous. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has pushed for "pacing" the development of increasingly powerful models on safety grounds, with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman among the AI leaders supporting greater caution.

However, the timing of the AI slowdown calls creates an uncomfortable financial question. The companies warning that frontier AI is moving too quickly are also among those spending most heavily to keep it moving quickly.

Of course, there is no evidence that OpenAI or Anthropic's financial obligations are driving their safety positions. But slowing the development cycle could have a second effect: giving both companies more time to earn money from today's models before paying for the next generation.

Promotion

AMZO: built for a short position on AMZN

OpenAI's Spending Commitments Dwarf Its Revenue

The ChatGPT maker generated about $13 billion in revenue in 2025, but spent roughly $34 billion, including $19 billion on research and development. It reported a net loss of about $39 billion, although roughly $30 billion came from a one-time accounting charge. Excluding major non-cash items, its operational loss was about $8 billion.

The spending continued in 2026. OpenAI burned $3.7 billion of cash in the first quarter on $5.7 billion of revenue and posted a $9.3 billion operating loss. Its reported net loss exceeded $21 billion, though that figure again included a large accounting charge.

More important for investors may be what comes next. OpenAI told shareholders it had an estimated $665 billion of computing spending commitments at the end of 2025, extending through 2030.

data.title: Micron Stock Wobbles as Taiwan Workers Reject 68 Months' Pay, Demand Profit-Sharing
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) stock rose in premarket trading on Tuesday even though workers at the chipmaker's Taiwan facilities rejected a record compensation package and continued to push for a permanent share of the company's profits. The labor dispute comes as Micron benefits from strong demand for AI memory chips used in data centers. Taiwan is a critical manufacturing hub for Micron, with about 15,000 employees on the island.

The unions have pointed to compensation arrangements at South Korean memory-chip makers Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) and SK Hynix (SKHY) as benchmarks. Micron workers are seeking a system that would allow employees to share more directly in the company's profitability during strong memory-market cycles.

Why Workers Are Pushing for Profit-Sharing

Micron recently announced fiscal 2026 rewards for its Taiwan employees equivalent to 35 to 68 months of pay. The package included an NT$1 million ($31,500) additional cash bonus for eligible employees who joined before August 29, 2025. Entry-level engineers were expected to receive average total rewards of about NT$3.4 million, including cash and equity.

However, Taiwan's Micron unions rejected the package, arguing that it does not address their broader demand for a permanent profit-sharing system. Specifically, the unions are seeking 15% of Micron's global operating profit to be allocated to employees.

Strike Risk Remains

No strike has been called, and there has been no reported impact on production so far. The dispute could become more significant if negotiations fail. The unions have said they could move toward a strike vote if Micron does not present a concrete proposal during mediation sessions scheduled for September 18 and 21.

Any disruption could raise concerns about supplies of DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which are increasingly important for AI infrastructure. It remains to be seen whether Micron can resolve the dispute without affecting production as demand for AI-related memory remains exceptionally strong.

data.title: Stock Market Today, September 15 – Futures Slip as Treasury Yields Cross 5%, Rate Hike Looms
data.description:
U.S. stock futures fell ahead of Tuesday's session as surging oil prices fueled renewed inflation concerns, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.03%. Investors are awaiting the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday. Markets are pricing in a 92% probability of a 0.25 percentage-point rate hike, which would raise the Fed's benchmark interest rate to 3.75%-4.00%.

Futures on the Nasdaq 100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were down 0.63%, 0.55%, and 0.67%, respectively, as of 5:38 a.m. EDT on September 15.

Oil prices extended gains on Tuesday as fresh attacks in the Gulf raised concerns about supply disruptions. Saudi Arabia also shut its key East-West oil pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, after drone attacks damaged it, further tightening supply. data.title: HOOD, MSTR, COIN: Crypto Stocks Slide Ahead of Senate CLARITY Act Vote
data.description:
Cryptocurrency stocks Robinhood (HOOD), Coinbase (COIN), and Strategy (MSTR) fell in premarket trading Tuesday ahead of a congressional vote on the CLARITY Act on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Bitcoin (BTC) was down nearly 2%, while Ethereum ($ETH-USD) fell 1.5%. Investors are also waiting for the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision, which could add to market volatility.

For context, the CLARITY Act aims to create a clearer regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies. The bill had previously faced delays over concerns about its safeguards against conflicts of interest and illicit finance.

Two Major Events Ahead for the Crypto Market

Investors are waiting for two key events in the next 24 hours. The Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points on Wednesday, which would lift its target range to 3.75%-4.00%.

Investors are also watching the Senate vote for clues about the future of digital asset rules. The vote could be an important test for the crypto market. If the bill fails to advance, investor sentiment could weaken, putting more pressure on digital assets. The Senate is set to vote on the CLARITY Act on Tuesday. The bill needs at least 60 votes to advance.

Recent weaker Bitcoin ETF inflows have added to the pressure on crypto stocks.

What the CLARITY Act Means for Crypto Companies

The CLARITY Act would aim to create clearer rules for cryptocurrency companies by defining how digital assets are regulated in the U.S. It could also clarify which regulators oversee different types of crypto assets and activities. This may give crypto companies more certainty as they build and expand their businesses.

It could help the crypto industry attract more institutional capital by giving asset managers, pension funds, and banks clearer rules for entering spot and derivatives markets. It could also encourage U.S. crypto companies to keep their projects and jobs in the country rather than moving offshore.

However, clearer rules could also raise costs for smaller startups. Companies may face higher legal, audit, and anti-money laundering compliance costs, along with stricter disclosure requirements.
